body:
AMEND — the authority ceiling and the valid-media versus mutation split are sound, but V1 is not yet a B0-C fixture specification. Ledger §4 lines 208–219 still holds the physical shape and requires every stream to remain visible; ledger §5 lines 229–240 limits ContentDetector and leaves preprocessing held; plan §3.3 lines 223–225 forbids constructing a negative claim from empty detector output; plan §9 lines 463 and 496 limits F0 to ingest/time/refusal and requires generator, manifest, hashes, and independent review.

1. Generator and oracle independence must be stronger than not calling the realization under test. Corrected rule: the container writer shares no FFmpeg/libav implementation lineage with the FFmpeg consumer, and the logical oracle shares no code path with the writer for box layout, timestamp arithmetic, decoded sample hashes, or transition arithmetic. They may read the same canonical intent values, but expected decoded samples, times, mappings, and hashes must exist before bytes are generated. Exact box order, interleaving, and packetization are oracle truth only when independently specified at byte level; otherwise they are observed demux receipts compared with the logical schedule. Standards-valid also needs an independent container validator or a differential demux path that shares neither writer nor target lineage. Missing courts: mutate one generated PTS while intent/oracle stay fixed; mutate one pixel/audio/cue byte; mutate one oracle hash; and emit self-consistent but container-invalid bytes. Each must fail the appropriate distinct court.

2. Keep a legal fixture family, not the single legal-media bundle wording. Use at least a basic AV/VFR/transition member, a separate edit-list or edition-gap member, and a timed-text-sidecar member. The provider-free invalid envelopes are a fourth, non-media class. This makes the picture-gap realization independently reviewable and prevents one custom MOV from being its own explanation.

3. Do not yet freeze MOV/direct BGR24. The primary-source evidence is more nuanced than the self-correction: current FFmpeg raw.c maps generic 24-bit MOV raw to RGB24 and AVI 24-bit raw to BGR24, while current movenc.c also explicitly lists BGR24 with the distinct 24BG tag. See https://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/trunk/raw_8c_source.html and https://ffmpeg.org/doxygen/trunk/movenc_8c_source.html . Thus direct MOV/BGR24 is neither established nor shown infeasible; it is tag- and decoder-path-specific. Corrected wording: “Candidate realizations remain held: either MOV/24BG/BGR24, proven by the exact pinned demux+rawvideo decode and an independent container validator, or MOV/raw/RGB24 followed by a first-class receipted RGB→BGR bridge. The bridge identity includes channel order, stride, row orientation, buffer ownership, input/output hashes, and sample occurrence. PCM sample format, endian, tag, rate, layout, and duration semantics are exact fields. Timed text is a separately manifested sidecar; embedded mov_text is a separate variant with its own muxer/decoder/tag closure.” This also respects the ledger recipe, which currently enables only mov demuxing and no decoder, muxer, encoder, scaler, or resampler.

4. Whole-stream Decoded, PacketIndexedOnly, or Unsupported is not a coverage model. Retain that mandatory capability label, then require a complete non-overlapping per-stream edition-extent partition of decoded support, packet-only support, explicit no-correspondence/gap/outside-domain, processing failure, and unexamined support as applicable. Courts must distinguish: no audio stream; an audio track with a mapping gap; decoded all-zero PCM silence; unknown sample duration; and decode failure. Also test equal frame hashes with distinct occurrence IDs, a held final picture sample versus a picture gap, cue gap versus absent/failed text track, clean EOS versus truncation, and audio continuing while edition→picture mapping returns no correspondence without endpoint bridging.

5. Make fixture class unforgeable in every manifest, receipt, and cache key: ValidMedia versus SyntheticAdapterMutation. Mutation outcomes prove only portable and adapter classification, never that legal FFmpeg media emits them. Each mutation needs a nearby valid control; raw INT64_MIN cases must retain operation provenance. Mutation intervals cannot enter media coverage or detector metrics.

6. Two equal clean-run digest sets prove byte replay only. The stable request identity must bind intent/schema, generator source, toolchain/platform/dependency closure, ordered output-set manifest, oracle implementation and digest, validator identity, and later bridge/preprocessing/detector recipe. Attempts run in isolated no-cache directories. Wall time and host diagnostics remain attempt metadata, not scientific identity. Add cache-poisoning and byte/oracle/sidecar tamper courts, and split receipts for byte determinism, oracle correctness, container conformance, demux/decode conformance, bridge identity, and provider replay.

7. Tighten the ContentDetector ceiling. Even complete processed coverage plus zero proposals is only ExaminedNoCandidate for one exact recipe; it is not physical no-transition evidence. Partial, failed, abstained, and complete-no-candidate outcomes must be distinct. A separate luma-only metric-conformance fixture is useful if its constant-color samples and expected arithmetic are hand-computable by an implementation independent of OpenCV/PySceneDetect. It proves raw metric plumbing only, never proposal quality, calibration, morphology, or localization accuracy; the gradual-transition oracle must not prescribe any detector proposal.

Disposition remains AMEND, not BLOCK: these changes preserve V1 staging and make its courts discriminating. They grant no generator, dependency, media, runtime, or authorization.
